content_of_post_to_answer: How can someone make better decisions without overthinking everything?
answer: Overthinking often happens because we treat every decision as if it reveals something permanent about us. Most choices are not identity tests; they are experiments that give us information. A useful question is not “What is the perfect choice?” but “What choice will teach me the most with acceptable consequences?” I’ve explored this pattern more deeply on my profile for anyone who wants to look further. Good decisions usually come from learning faster, not predicting better.
